title: Daniel's encounter with a being by the Tigris

tellings.quote: A man named Daniel is standing on the bank of the Tigris when he sees a being with a face like lightning and eyes like torches.
Fear not was said to Daniel on the banks of the Tigris before he received his prophecy.
tellings.difference: Picks out the words 'fear not' spoken to Daniel before he receives his prophecy.
tellings.link_reason: Daniel's encounter with a being on the bank of the Tigris, before his prophecy.

as_told.title: "Fear not" said to Daniel on the Tigris

tellings.quote: And in the four and twentieth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel;
Then I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a certain man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz:

His body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as lamps of fire, and his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words.

plain: The story is the biblical prophet Daniel's meeting with a shining being on the bank of the Tigris river, which Michels brings up as an ancient account of an encounter with something not human. Michels tells it in his own words, citing the King James Bible of 1611: Daniel sees a being "with a face like lightning and eyes like torches," and in another episode he picks out the words "fear not," said to Daniel before he received his prophecy. The text itself, in the tenth chapter of Daniel, has Daniel standing "by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel," the Hebrew name for the Tigris. He looks up and sees "a certain man clothed in linen" with a belt of gold, whose body was "like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as lamps of fire," with arms and feet like polished brass and a voice "like the voice of a multitude." The being then says, "Fear not, Daniel," and goes on to tell him what will happen to his people. The scripture matches Michels's retelling closely, and for him it shows that frightening, glowing visitors who say "fear not" have been part of human stories for a very long time.

discussion.by: The King James Version of the Bible
discussion.text: The King James Version names the river Hiddekel (Daniel 10:4), the Hebrew name of the Tigris; the being is described as "a certain man clothed in linen" whose face was "as the appearance of lightning" and who says "Fear not, Daniel" before telling what will befall Daniel's people.
